brief.subject: Family Dollar to pay $63 million over register overcharges
brief.headline: Family Dollar to Pay $63 Million Over Shelf-Price Overcharges; FTC Targets Vet Merger
brief.dek: Regulators settle a register-pricing case, sue to stop a vet-supply merger, and add states to a telehealth billing and privacy suit.
brief.lede: Family Dollar will pay $63 million to settle FTC and state claims that shoppers were charged more at checkout than the posted prices.

sections.heading: Family Dollar settles overcharge claims
bullets: $63 million: Family Dollar's payment to settle claims from the FTC and 17 states.
Regulators allege registers routinely rang up higher than shelf tags, price stickers and ads showed.
Officials say the gap cost shoppers millions of dollars, so compare your receipt to the posted price.

sections.heading: FTC sues to block vet-supply merger
bullets: $3.5 billion: Covetrus's planned purchase of rival MWI Veterinary Supply, which the FTC sued to stop.
The FTC says the two are the largest veterinary product distributors.
The agency warns a combination could raise costs for vet clinics and, in turn, pet owners.

sections.heading: More states join Hims and Hers suit
bullets: Five states joined as co-plaintiffs in an amended FTC complaint against telehealth firm Hims and Hers.
The FTC alleges the company misled users about billing and cancellation practices.
It also alleges sensitive health data went to ad platforms despite privacy promises.

items.title: Five States Join FTC Lawsuit Alleging Hims and Hers Engaged in Deceptive and Unlawful Privacy Practices
items.snippet: The Federal Trade Commission filed an amended complaint adding five states as co-plaintiffs in its lawsuit alleging that telehealth provider Hims and Hers shared consumers’ sensitive health information with third-party advertising platforms, despite claiming its services maintain consumers’ privacy, and it deceived users about its billing and cancellation practices.
